  "output": "# once-campfire-rust

Campfire, the chat app, in Rust. It runs existing Rails Campfire installs
([basecamp/once-campfire](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire)) without migrating data.

- Stay compatible with existing installs unless told otherwise: the SQLite schema, the storage
  layout, and signed/encrypted cookies (so people stay signed in across an upgrade).
- List behavior that differs from Rails Campfire under "Known differences" in `README.md`.

## Layout

| Path | Package | What |
|---|---|---|
| `bin/` | — | `dev`: local server and seed |
| `crates/ruby` | `ruby_compat` | Ruby's own string behaviour the other crates share (ERB escaping, `String#to_i`/`#to_f`/`#strip`, `Float#to_s`, `CGI.escape`, `ERB::Util.url_encode`, Active Record's integer binding, Rack's byte ranges), checked by `vectors/ruby_core.json`; no dependencies |
| `crates/rails_compat` | `rails_compat` | Rails signing/encryption/serialization contracts and the Rails formats several crates write (`ActiveSupport::JSON`, `Content-Disposition`), checked by `vectors/`, and the app's `Clock` (`Time.current`, and time travel for tests) |
| `crates/kit` | `campfire_kit` | Axum adapter, `Ctx`, params, cookies, session, forgery protection, flash, formats, responses, gzip, and the front server (TLS, ACME, HTTP/2, response cache) |
| `crates/routes` | `campfire_routes` | Path helpers for the app's routes |
| `crates/db` | `campfire_db` | rusqlite over the schema, models, queries, fixtures (`fixtures/`) and their loader |
| `crates/richtext` | `campfire_richtext` | Rich text content pipeline: sanitize, attachments, autolink, plain text |
| `crates/storage` | `campfire_storage` | Active Storage-compatible blobs, disk service, variants (libvips), previews (ffmpeg) |
| `crates/cable` | `campfire_cable` | Action Cable protocol server, its WebSocket implementation, and in-process pub/sub |
| `crates/assets` | `campfire_assets` | The frontend (`app/`, `vendor/`, `public/`, `importmap.rb`), digested and embedded at build time |
| `crates/views` | `campfire_views` | Askama templates and view helpers |
| `crates/campfire` | `campfire` (bin) | Controllers, router wiring, channels, jobs, integrations, seeds |
| `vectors/` | — | Frozen test data (recorded from Rails and Ruby) and `test.env`, the fixed test-only keys |
| `bench/` | — | Load generator, benchmark scripts and recorded results |

## Working rules

- Rust comes from mise if it isn't on the PATH: `mise exec rust@1.98.1 -- cargo ...` (the version
  in `Dockerfile`).
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude html5ever` runs everything. The app's integration tests build
  their seed databases themselves.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude html5ever --all-targets` should stay clean. (`html5ever` is a
  vendored copy with one backported fix and two small additions for Gumbo's parse limits, all
  recorded in its `Cargo.toml`, and identical to upstream otherwise.)
- Format with `cargo fmt --all` (`rustfmt.toml`) before committing, and `bench/loadgen`, a workspace
  of its own, with `cargo fmt --manifest-path bench/loadgen/Cargo.toml`; CI checks both. The
  vendored html5ever has its own `rustfmt.toml` that turns formatting off, and generated tables are
  marked `#[rustfmt::skip]`.
- CI also runs `cargo shear` for dependencies declared but not used. When it can't see a real use
  (a build script's `#[path]` modules, a self dev-dependency), list the crate under
  `[package.metadata.cargo-shear] ignored` in that manifest, with the reason.
- Put shared dependency versions in the root `[workspace.dependencies]`, and reference them with
  `foo.workspace = true`.
- Frontend changes go in `crates/assets/app/`. `crates/assets/vendor/` holds third-party
  JavaScript and CSS, copied byte-for-byte (see its `MANIFEST.md`); don't edit it.
- Write code that reads like the surrounding code: small, clearly named functions, and comments
  only where the behavior is non-obvious. Say why when behavior deliberately differs from Rails
  Campfire.
- Tests live beside the code. Golden-vector tests read `vectors/*.json`.
- Performance changes come with before-and-after measurements, recorded under `bench/results/`.
# How to contribute to Campfire in Rust

This repository uses GitHub
[discussions](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire-rust/discussions) to track feature
requests and questions, rather than [the issue
tracker](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire-rust/issues). If you're considering opening an
issue or pull request, please open a discussion instead.

Whenever a discussion leads to an actionable and well-understood task, we'll move it to the issue
tracker where it can be worked on.

## What this means in practice

### If you'd like to contribute to the code...

1. If you're interested in working on one of the open issues, please do! We are grateful for the
   help!
2. Make sure someone else isn't already working on the same issue. If they are, it will be tagged
   "in progress" and/or it should be clear from the comments. When in doubt, comment on the issue
   to ask.
3. Read [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) for the layout and working rules: how to build and test, what has
   to stay compatible with existing installs, and where differences from Rails Campfire are
   recorded.
4. When you have something ready for review or collaboration, run `cargo fmt --all` and open a PR.
   CI checks the formatting and runs clippy and the tests.

### If you've found a bug...

1. If you don't have steps to reproduce the problem, or you're not certain it's a bug, open a
   discussion.
2. If you have steps to reproduce, open an issue. If it's a security issue, see
   [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) instead.

### If you have an idea for a feature...

1. Open a discussion.

### If you have a question, or are having trouble with configuration...

1. Open a discussion.

Thanks for helping! ❤️
# Chat bots

Bots aren't in Rails Campfire as this app ports it. Any member can set them up. Administrators
manage everyone's.

## Data

- A bot is a `users` row with `role = 2` (`Role::Bot`), so it joins rooms, has memberships and
  authors messages like a person. `User::create` grants it every open room after commit.
- Its `bots` row (`campfire_db::Bot`, created by `schema::ADDITIONS`) holds `user_id` (unique),
  `creator_id` and `token`. It's a separate table rather than columns on `users`:
  `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is idempotent on every boot, `users` keeps the Rails columns that
  `columns_test` checks, and the Rails image ignores it.
- The bot code is `"<user id>-<token>"` (Rails Campfire's `bot_key` format). The token has 24
  alphanumeric characters. `Bot::authenticate` looks the bot up by id and compares tokens with
  `rails_compat::secure_compare`.
- `password_digest` is `NOT NULL`, so a bot gets the bcrypt digest of a random password. It has no
  email address, so it can't sign in, and session transfers refuse bots.
- Deleting a bot deletes its `bots` row and deactivates its user, so its messages keep their author.
  Resetting a code (`PATCH /bots/:bot_id/key`) replaces the token.

## Routes

`controllers::app_routes` holds routes Rails doesn't have. They're matched after the whole Rails
table, which stays identical to `vectors/campfire_routes.json`. The route tests seed their corpus
from both tables.

| Route | Action |
|---|---|
| `GET /bots`, `GET /bots/new`, `POST /bots` | list (no pagination, `Cache-Control: no-store`), form, create |
| `GET /bots/:id/edit`, `PATCH/PUT /bots/:id`, `DELETE /bots/:id` | edit, rename/avatar, delete |
| `PATCH/PUT /bots/:bot_id/key` | new code |
| `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages` | the bot API (`messages::by_bots`) |

Bots someone can't manage answer 404 (`Bot::find_manageable_by`).

## The bot API

- The chain skips session authentication and forgery protection. `concerns::authenticate_bot`
  returns 401, then `set_room` returns 404 (an unknown room, or one the bot isn't in). A blank body
  without a multipart `attachment` gets 422. Success is `201` with `Location: /messages/:id`, a path.

steps.message:
Webhooks for bots work: when someone mentions a bot in a message, its webhook is called with the JSON payload from the story, and a text or HTML answer is posted into the room as the bot's message. The test suite passes except one storage test (`pipeline_matches_the_vectors` in `crates/storage`). It fails because video preview images come out a few bytes different from the recorded ones, which is most likely this machine's ffmpeg version. Nothing I changed touches that code.

I couldn't run `cargo fmt` or `cargo clippy` because the toolchain here doesn't have them and there's no network to install them. I kept lines under the 140-character limit by hand; please run both before merging.

**The form.** Both the new-bot and edit pages have a "Webhook URL" field, a real `<label>` around the input. Saving it empty removes the webhook. A form that doesn't send the field at all leaves the webhook alone. Anything that isn't an `http://` or `https://` URL with a host is rejected with a 422 and the error "Webhook url must be an http:// or https:// URL".

**Storage.** The URL lives in a new `bot_webhooks` table, created on boot like the existing `bots` table. I didn't add a column to `bots` because databases that already have that table wouldn't get it. Deleting a bot deletes its webhook.

**The call.** Posting a message never waits for a bot:
- The call runs in the background on its own job queue, so a slow bot only holds up other bots.
- A test with a bot that takes 3 seconds to answer confirms posting stays quick.
- Each mentioned bot with a webhook gets the payload as specified. `text` has its own `@Name` removed, `reply_to` is its own posting URL, `link` points to the message, and all paths are relative. For direct rooms, which have no name, `room.name` is the room's display name.
- The author is never called about their own message.

**The answer.**
- **`200` with `text/plain`:** escaped and posted, with line breaks kept.
- **`200` with `text/html`:** posted as rich text, cleaned up when shown like any message.
- **Anything else:** `204`, other success codes, other content types and empty bodies post nothing.
- **Errors:** failures and timeouts (7 seconds to connect or read, 15 overall) are only logged; nothing is posted to the room.
- **Size limit:** answers over 1 MB are dropped.

**Mention autocomplete.** Bots already appeared there, since they're room members, so I only added a test for it.

Decisions for you:
- **Only messages posted by people call webhooks.** Messages from the bot API, including bots' own answers, don't, so two bots can't loop by mentioning each other. The catch is that bots can't talk to each other through mentions.
- **Webhooks can reach any address, including `localhost` and the local network.** Push notifications and link previews block those, but bots often run next to Campfire, and QA's receiver will likely be local. The catch is that any member who can set up a bot can make the server send requests inside your network and see text answers in the room. Blocking private addresses later is a small change.

The main code is in `controllers/messages/bot_webhooks.rs`, `integrations/webhooks.rs` and the new `campfire_db::Webhook` model. The request-level tests are in `controllers/bots/tests.rs`. Design notes are in `docs/bots.md` (new "Webhooks" section), and the bots entry in the README now mentions webhooks.
